project: QTS Cedar Rapids campus at Big Cedar Industrial Center, 76th Avenue SW

documents.title: City Council agenda, December 2, 2025 (amended and restated agreement, item 6)
The Gazette: city would rebate $529 million to data center
KCRG: mayor defends data center projects amid NDA questions

community_fund.controlled_by: The City, for growth of amenities; the company gets input.
community_fund.notes: Community Betterment Fund: $300,000 a year per phase for up to 20 years, starting the fiscal year the City first receives tax increment from that phase, capped at $6M per phase and $18M total. The developer may prepay at an 8 percent net present value discount, and may withhold payment if the City fails to appropriate the grants.

clawbacks.notes: Forward-looking only. If a phase has fewer than 15 full-time employees, the City skips the next grant and the next franchise-fee rebate for that phase. A job shortfall is expressly not an event of default. No repayment of grants already paid, and no trigger tied to the facility ceasing operation. Failure to build is an event of default allowing suspension or termination after a 60-day cure.

decommissioning.notes: No decommissioning term in the agreement.

grid_costs.governed_by: Alliant Energy large-customer rate; terms not public
grid_costs.notes: The agreement is silent on electric costs and references a separate electrical service agreement only as a permitted excuse for delay. Alliant says data centers pay for their own equipment under a specific rate with long-term commitments, and QTS signed a federal ratepayer protection pledge. None of that is in the city deal.

water.notes: The agreement has no cap and no reporting. QTS states it uses closed-loop air-cooled chillers and consumes no water for cooling once operational. The City builds water main and sewer to the property and paves 76th Avenue; QTS pays about $13M in sewer and $3.8M in water connection costs. Linn County sought a $20,000 penalty from a contractor for 40 unpermitted dewatering wells at the site in 2025.

noise.notes: No noise term in the agreement.

jobs.notes: At least 15 full-time employees per completed phase, where full time means 30 hours a week at the state laborshed wage. Certified annually each November 1 without names. The only consequence is a skipped grant. Construction job figures are projections.

local_contracting.notes: A separate Linn County road-use agreement in October 2025 covers about $117,000 in back payment, paving of two rural roads, and a performance bond for two others. Also a 75 percent rebate of electric franchise fees for 20 years per data center, which runs the other direction.

transparency.notes: The City signed nondisclosure agreements with QTS and Google, obtained by public records request in July 2026. The agreement has a confidentiality clause subject to Iowa open records law. The executed agreement is posted online. No dashboard and no audit; one annual meeting between City and developer.

tax.notes: Twenty annual economic development grants per phase equal to 70 percent of the tax increment, paid from TIF only and subject to annual appropriation. The owners may not seek other exemptions or convert to tax-exempt status. City estimate: about $1B in total property tax, about $529M rebated. No but-for analysis was found.

criticisms.summary: The City signed NDAs with both data center companies, disclosed only through a records request; the mayor denied kickback accusations.
The amended agreement passed in December 2025 with no public comment.
Energy advocates raised unanswered questions on water and power impacts.
